entries.title: CS50x Curriculum: Comprehensive Week-by-Week Syllabus | CS50x Hub
entries.content:
Skip to main content

CS50x Curriculum Breakdown

Harvard CS50x is structured across 11 core weeks of progressive difficulty:

Week Topic Core Concepts Primary Language
Week 0 Computational Thinking Binary, ASCII, algorithms, pseudocode, Scratch Scratch
Week 1 C Programming Types, variables, conditionals, loops, CLI compilation C (clang)
Week 2 Arrays & Strings Memory layout, strings as char arrays, cryptography C
Week 3 Algorithms Linear/Binary search, Bubble/Merge sort, Big O notation C
Week 4 Memory & Pointers Heap vs Stack, pointers, malloc, free, Valgrind, file I/O C
Week 5 Data Structures Linked lists, hash tables, tries, binary search trees C
Week 6 Python Syntax, dynamic typing, dictionaries, list comprehensions Python 3
Week 7 SQL & Databases Relational modeling, primary/foreign keys, joins, indexes SQLite
Week 8 HTML, CSS & JS DOM events, responsive layouts, asynchronous fetch JavaScript / CSS
Week 9 Flask Web Apps MVC, HTTP requests (GET/POST), sessions, Jinja templates Python / Flask
Week 10 Cybersecurity & Ethics Buffer overflows, SQL injection, XSS, responsible disclosure C / Security

entries.title: Academic Honesty & Ethical Collaboration Policy | CS50x Hub
entries.content:
Skip to main content

Academic Honesty & Collaboration Policy

CS50x Hub strictly adheres to the principle that true learning requires active problem solving.

What is Encouraged:

  • Discussing algorithmic approaches in high-level pseudocode.
  • Explaining C syntax, compiler warnings, and Valgrind outputs.
  • Creating conceptual mental models and memory diagrams.

What is Prohibited:

  • Sharing or publishing complete problem set source code.
  • Soliciting or viewing exact line-by-line solutions before completing your own work.

Frequently Asked Questions

Questions? Answers.

How long does it take to complete CS50x?

Most students spend 10 to 20 hours per week over 10 to 12 weeks. Because the course is self-paced, you can progress according to your own schedule.

Is the Harvard certificate free?

Yes. Students who earn a score of 70% or higher on every required assignment receive a free, downloadable CS50 Certificate of Completion from CS50 directly.

entries.title: Developer Guides: Valgrind, GDB & Memory Management | CS50x Hub
entries.content:
Skip to main content

Developer Guides: Debugging & Memory Management

1. Mastering Valgrind for Memory Leak Elimination

When working with dynamic heap allocations (malloc, calloc, realloc), memory leaks occur when allocated blocks lose all pointer references before being passed to free().

Diagnostic Command

valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --track-origins=yes ./speller texts/shakespeare.txt

Common Valgrind Error Types

  1. Invalid read/write of size N: Attempting to access memory before or after an allocated buffer (buffer overflow/underflow).
  2. Conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value(s): Reading a variable before assigning it an initial value.
  3. Definitely lost: Heap memory that was allocated and never freed with no remaining pointer pointing to it.

2. Big O Asymptotic Complexity Cheatsheet

Algorithm / Data Structure Search Time Insert Time Space Complexity
Array (Unsorted) O(n) O(1) amortized O(n)
Array (Sorted / Binary Search) O(log n) O(n) O(n)
Linked List O(n) O(1) O(n)
Hash Table O(1) average / O(n) worst O(1) average O(n)
Trie (Prefix Tree) O(k) where k is word length O(k) O(k * alphabet_size)

Transitioning from C to Python, relational databases, SQLite queries, HTML5/CSS, client JavaScript DOM manipulation, Flask MVC, and security fundamentals.

entries.title: Problem Set Guidance & Conceptual Strategies | CS50x Hub
entries.content:
Skip to main content

Problem Set Strategies & Conceptual Models

Mastering the most challenging assignments in the CS50x curriculum.

1. Tideman (Week 3: Ranked Pairs Voting)

  • Concept: Graph theory, directed acyclic graphs (DAG), cycle detection using Depth-First Search (DFS).
  • Key Strategy: Before locking an edge [winner -> loser], run a recursive check to see if loser can already reach winner. If a path exists, adding the edge creates a cycle and must be skipped.

2. Filter (Week 4: Image Processing in C)

  • Concept: 2D pixel arrays, RGB triplets, edge detection with Sobel kernels.
  • Key Strategy: Always allocate a temporary buffer when applying blur or edge filters so modified adjacent pixel values do not corrupt subsequent calculations in the same pass.

3. Speller (Week 5: Dictionary Spell Checker)

  • Concept: Hash tables, collision resolution via linked lists, memory leak elimination with valgrind.
  • Key Strategy: Design a fast, uniform hash function (e.g. polynomial rolling hash or DJB2) to minimize bucket chain length. Ensure every allocated node is freed recursively in unload().

4. C$50 Finance (Week 9: Full-Stack Stock Portfolio)

  • Concept: SQL transactions, session authentication, real-time stock API quote lookups, CSRF protection.
  • Key Strategy: Enforce atomicity when executing buy/sell operations: balance updates and transaction ledger inserts must occur within a single database transaction block.
